hints: A valid flight route visits every city exactly once, so fix city 1 as the start and city n as the finish.
Use a bitmask for the set of intermediate cities already visited and the current endpoint.
When all intermediate cities are used, count a route only if the final edge reaches n.
analogy: Track which cities have already been visited; from each state, try an unvisited next city.
example: For n=3 with flights 1->2 and 2->3, exactly one route visits all cities from 1 to 3.
algorithm: Let dp[mask][u] count paths from 1 that visit mask and end at u. Extend over unvisited outgoing neighbors; when mask contains 1..n-1, add edges to n. Use modulo 1e9+7.
correctness: Every Hamiltonian route has a unique visited-set and endpoint at each step; the transitions enumerate all such prefixes once and only complete them with a final edge to n.
complexity: O(2^n*m) time and O(2^n*n) space; exploit n<=20 and store only masks that include start.
